title: Membrane Technology
evidence_note: No outline available, but the CLOs are unusually specific and name the technique, its mechanisms and its failure modes directly. Mapped with confidence on CLO evidence alone - contrast with CHE-344, whose generic CLOs permitted no mapping.

mapped.evidence: CLO-1: classify membranes based on materials and preparation methods. CLO-2: Interpret the membrane transport mechanisms and distinguish different membrane modules for their separation performance. CLO-3: identify membrane process problems (polarization and fouling).

CLO-2 (C-6): Apply the engineering concepts for selection, specification and design of process equipment. Vessel design; low-, medium-, and high-pressure storage and transportation vessels; cryogenic vessels; design codes, standards, and materials selection.
Process design and development, process flow sheeting, flow diagrams, PFD and P&ID, equipment and instrument symbols.
CLO-3: Compute and Analyze the costing, profitability, and safety parameters of a chemical process plant. Economic evaluation and optimization: basic concepts of cost indexing.
Hazards identification and risk assessment: process hazards checklists and surveys, safety reviews. CLO-3 includes safety parameters of a chemical process plant.
Rotating equipment including pumps, motors, compressors, and turbines.
General design considerations; design codes, standards, and materials selection.
Piping and pipeline design.
Design ethics: local and global impact analysis.
Heat transfer equipment including furnaces and refrigeration units.
Hazards identification and risk assessment: process hazards checklists and surveys, safety reviews.
Material transport; material handling.

title: Chemical Process Design & Simulation
evidence_note: Outline taken from CHE-454.md under the confirmed renumbering.

mapped.evidence: CLO-3 (C-6): Design and evaluate a plant wide model of a process industry. CLO-1: Compute process flowsheets comprising pump, compressor, reactor, distillation column in Aspen HYSYS. Contents: fluid packages, PFDs in HYSYS, simulation of heat transfer, separators, pressure changers and reactors.
Linear programming application to chemical processes in multi-variant situations; unconstrained functions with one-dimensional search; nonlinear mixed-integer optimization.
Importance and hierarchy of optimization: significance of optimization in chemical engineering; classification and model development; solution and interpretation of optimization models.
Hierarchy of process design; process synthesis and design strategy; strategies for decision making.
Economic analysis in the simulation environment; economic and time value of objective functions.
CLO-2: Analyze dynamic mode of process models for temperature, pressure, flowrate, and composition control loops.
Steady-state material and energy balances using the graphical user interface and worksheet.
Application of optimization in heat transfer and energy conservation.

title: Computational Fluid Dynamics in Chemical Engineering
evidence_note: Outline taken from CHE-433.md under the confirmed renumbering.

mapped.evidence: CLO-1 (C-5): Develop 2D/3D fluid-flow models by using CFD software. CLO-2 (C-6): Generate hydrodynamic profiles via CFD-Post processing. Contents: RANS, large eddy simulation, direct numerical simulation; finite volume method; SIMPLE algorithm.
The finite volume method for convection and diffusion problems; the power-law scheme; TVD schemes; the hybrid differencing scheme; discretized forms and solution methodologies.
Conservation laws of fluid motion and boundary conditions; the continuity equation and governing equations for momentum, heat, and mass transport in a continuum.
The general transport equation; governing equations for momentum, heat and mass transport.
Discretized forms and solution methodologies for steady- and unsteady-state one-dimensional heat conduction; extension to two- and three-dimensional domains.
